sections.title: How much you’ll be paid
sections.html: Up to 100% of actual costs for each training course

sections.title: How this item benefits the environment
sections.html: Training to control and manage non-native plant species will help you understand how to manage the harm these plants cause to the natural environment.

sections.title: Where you can use this item
sections.html:
With the approval of Natural England (or the Forestry Commission for woodland), you can only use this item alongside one of the following:

  • CSP13: Invasive plant species control and management (lower rate)
  • CSP14: Invasive plant species control and management (intermediate rate)
  • CSP15: Invasive plant species control and management (upper rate)

sections.title: What you must do to use this item
sections.html:
You must: 

  • find relevant training courses on how to control and manage invasive plant species
  • provide a species management plan approved by Natural England or the Forestry Commission with your application
  • provide at least 2 written quotations for the course costs with your application (where possible)
  • agree which training course you will attend with Natural England or the Forestry Commission
  • attend and complete a training course

If you can only find one suitable course, you can attend that course with the agreement of your Natural England or Forestry Commission adviser.

sections.title: Evidence you must keep
sections.html:
You must keep and provide with your claim:

  • evidence that you have completed the training course (for example, a certificate or email from the training provider)
  • receipted invoices, or bank statements where a receipted invoice is not available, for the training course

Read the record keeping and site visit requirements in the Agreement holder’s guide: Capital Grants, Higher Tier capital grants and Protection and Infrastructure grants for more information.

If you’re applying for this item as part of a Countryside Stewardship Higher Tier (CSHT) application, read the record keeping and site visit requirements in the CSHT agreement holder’s guide.

sections.title: Other items you can use with this item
sections.html:
Capital plans

You can use this item with these plans:

  • PA2: Feasibility study

  • PA3: Woodland management plan

  • PA7: Species management plan

Capital items

You can use this item with these items:

  • FM2: Carry out customised capital works to manage specific sites or species

  • SM6: Use monitoring equipment to manage invasive species

sections.title: Advice to help you use this item
sections.html:
The following advice may help you to use this item, but you do not have to follow it to get paid. It’s not part of this item’s requirements.   

You advisor will work with you to determine the most appropriate management approach for the invasive non-native plant species that occur on your land. For some species, the most appropriate approach may include chemical control, which may require a NPTC PA1 and PA6 qualification. Speak to your advisors about training opportunities that may be available.

If you’re applying for this item as part of a Countryside Stewardship Higher Tier (CSHT) application, you must read the CSHT applicant’s guide to understand the rules and how to apply.

How much you’ll be paid

How this item benefits the environment

If you can only find one suitable course, you can attend that course with the agreement of your Natural England or Forestry Commission adviser.

  • receipted invoices, or bank statements where a receipted invoice is not available, for the training course

Read the record keeping and site visit requirements in the Agreement holder’s guide: Capital Grants, Higher Tier capital grants and Protection and Infrastructure grants for more information.
